measured_rule: Warehouse-ferry with autonomous porter NPCs, on a 16x16 block grid (4x4 cells per block). Measured mechanics: (1) moving into an adjacent box marks it (border 4→3) without displacing the player; 5 then picks it (border→0) and the box stays glued at its pick-time offset (player→box direction) through all subsequent moves, so to push a box east you must pick it from its west side; 5 drops it in place (border→3) and the player must STEP AWAY one block to release it (border 3→4) — a rival will never take a border-3 box (measured in probe16: rival walked to the planted box and waited indefinitely until release). (2) Rivals advance exactly 1 block per player action of any kind (lockstep world tick, including on interact/idles); they autonomously target the nearest reachable released box, drag it trailing behind them, deposit it into a free dock slot, then seek the next target, parking when none remains; a new released box wakes a parked rival instantly. (3) {1,2}-speckle walls block the player even through an open gap (measured: move into open socket = no-op except timer), but a carried box CAN be pushed into a speckle-wall block ('planted'), where a rival on the far side can fetch it — this is the only way to move boxes across walls. (4) Score increments exactly when the last box on the board is docked (L3: 5th box docked → score 2→3 with 24 idle actions of rival ferry time). Level designs: L1 = 3 boxes, player alone docks them into a 3-slot dock. L2 = 5 boxes, 6-slot dock, one rival competes/helps (player docks 2, rival docks 3 in the verified program). L3 = wall splits the board; player side has 3 boxes, rival side has the 12-slot-approach dock; wall has two plug boxes the rival first extracts and docks, opening sockets; player feeds its 3 boxes through the sockets (plant + release), rival ferries all 5 to the dock. L4 (recon only) = same loop generalized: player sealed in a speckle-walled room with 6 boxes, 3 rivals and ~7 scattered dock slots outside; measured that planting into an arbitrary wall block works and a rival fetched and docked it.

A parity counter increments on EVERY move and click, but the flood advances one cell only on lateral moves that end with zero rise (including bumps) when post-increment parity is even; death when the player's row equals the flood row at that check. measured_rule: Balloon-corridor climber ("rise-until-blocked" maze). Actions available: 3=left, 4=right, 6=click, 7=undo, 0=reset (no up/down/interact). Moving laterally into a passable cell (empty, toggle-open '2', or flood-surface 'm') makes the balloon then rise (or fall, when gravity is flipped) until blocked; moving into anything else is a bump. Rising/falling onto a spike ('v'/'u') = death; reaching the gem '+' laterally or by rise = level complete. Clicks: a door 'x' is removed; toggle '1'<->'2' flips per-cell (solid<->open); a gravity button 'g' clicked anywhere on screen flips the global rise/fall direction, is consumed, and immediately re-floats/drops the player; a spread 'y' is removed and spawns blockers in its 4 empty neighbours; clicks on anything else are no-ops that still burn budget and parity (useful for flood-parity control). Measured quirk: clicking the cell directly above (grav-up) / below (grav-down) the player launches the player through that cell, with the traverse path evaluated BEFORE the clicked cell's new state — so clicking a door or even a toggle directly above both actuates it and moves you through it; used in every verified program. Click coordinates map as cell=(x//6,(y+camera_y)//6) with camera_y=py*6-36 (up) / py*6-26 (down); reachable click band is roughly cy-py in [-6..4] (up) / [-4..5] (down).
